summary.prose: The daemon stops opening every repository's saved connections when it starts, so starting it never touches the macOS Keychain and its socket opens immediately. A repository's saved connections are opened the first time a connection-management request needs them, using the existing per-repository opener that remembers a success and retries after a failure. A first-time set-up that the Keychain refuses now leaves nothing on disk, so the next request simply retries, and a Keychain refusal reaches the client as the existing 'secret-unavailable' error instead of 'recovery-required'. Reducing the number of Keychain prompts to one per run is a separate later Story (user decision 'A', 2026-11-05).

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Bugfix ISSUE-fefa97b991537da7, narrowed scope (user decision "A": split). This Story = ON-DEMAND OPENING ONLY: (1) remove the daemon boot loop (src/daemon/index.ts:455-461) that calls ensureDefaultManagedRoot for every registered repo before server.listen, so a daemon start triggers no Keychain reads; (2) open a repository's managed root on its first connection-management use, via the existing memoised ensureDefaultManagedRoot (src/daemon/db/management-defaults.ts) at every main-thread reader of savedManagementFor (connection-management-rpc.ts owner/safeList/capabilities, db-rpc.ts listConnections/upsert/removal); (3) make initializeFreshManagedRoot obtain the ticket key (SavedTicketAuthority.open) before any disk write, so a refused Keychain read leaves no partial state; (4) propagate keystore failure causes so managementRejection reports the existing 'secret-unavailable' code instead of 'recovery-required'. The db_* data tools (withDriver -> acquirePool -> DriverPool.reload -> loadConnections, secrets resolved per connection at driver build) never depended on the boot-time open and stay unchanged. The one-prompt-per-run connection vault is a SEPARATE later Story and a non-goal here.

api.name: ensureDefaultManagedRoot

parameters.name: root
parameters.purpose: Registered repository whose saved management a request needs.

parameters.name: ports
parameters.purpose: Unchanged registration, keystore and enablement seams; the request handlers use the default (lookupRepoId).

returns.meaning: Unchanged contract: resolves once savedManagementFor(root) is installed; memoised per root; a rejected attempt is forgotten so the next call retries. What changes is who calls it: no longer the boot loop, now the main-thread request handlers listed in dataModel.

errors.condition: The Keychain refused or failed reading or creating the root's ticket key (existing mapping in SavedTicketAuthority.open).
A rollback-copy or connection-secret read inside openManagedRoot was refused or failed in the Keychain.
A legacy unmanaged registry (offline adoption needed), damaged metadata, or any non-keystore integrity failure; unchanged.

preconditions: Called on the daemon main thread only (db.* and db.connections.v2.* methods), where the owners memo lives.
postconditions: No call is made before server.listen.
closeDefaultManagedRoots still closes every root opened on demand at shutdown.

api.name: initializeFreshManagedRoot

parameters.name: root
parameters.purpose: Registered repository with no registry and no management marker.

returns.meaning: Unchanged result. Changed order: after the existing uid/realpath/registration, enablement, absent-registry and no-marker checks, it generates registryId and calls SavedTicketAuthority.open({ adopted: false }) BEFORE the first filesystem write (parent mkdir/chmod, privateDirectory, proveWriterFence, state-directory mkdir, snapshot, preparing.json). The generated registryId is the one written to preparing.json, the state file and the registry envelope.

errors.condition: The Keychain refused creating or reading back the new ticket key; nothing has been written to disk, and no management marker exists, so the next ensureDefaultManagedRoot runs a clean initialization.

Any later step fails as today; in addition the freshly created ticket key for the abandoned registryId is deleted best-effort (a failed delete is logged by ref name only and leaves only an unused Keychain item).

preconditions: The legacy-registry refusal (before.missing check and managementMarkerExists) still runs before any Keychain access, so a legacy repository never touches the Keychain.
postconditions: A Keychain refusal leaves no state directory, snapshot, preparing.json or registry on disk.

api.name: managementRejection

parameters.name: error
parameters.purpose: Any error raised by a management path.

returns.meaning: As today, except: when the error is a KeystoreUnavailableError, or its `cause` is one, the code is 'secret-unavailable' with message 'Connection credentials are unavailable.'.

postconditions: No secret value and no ref value appears in code or message; only the fixed message for the code.

api.name: ManagedStoreError
api.signature: class ManagedStoreError extends Error { constructor(code: 'registry-unreadable' | 'recovery-required' | 'reconciliation-required' | 'unsupported-filesystem', options?: ErrorOptions | undefined) }

parameters.name: options
parameters.purpose: New optional standard `cause`, used only to carry a KeystoreUnavailableError.

returns.meaning: Unchanged code and message; internal recovery semantics (assertReady, journal pending, retry) are unchanged.

postconditions: Existing callers that pass only a code are unaffected.

dataModelChanges.details: Internal marker `class KeystoreUnavailableError extends Error` (name only, fixed message 'keystore unavailable', the original keytar error as `cause` for debugging; never serialised to a client). Thrown by a small wrapper around the keystore port calls that management code makes: CredentialGenerations.current (src/daemon/db/secrets.ts:210), the staged-value reads and writes in stageSnapshot (:272 and the setKey staging loop), and openManagedRoot's rollback-copy read (src/daemon/db/management-startup.ts:53) and enabled() secret reads (:85). A returned null is NOT a keystore failure and keeps its existing recovery-required meaning. The catch sites at src/daemon/db/secrets.ts:212, :236, :242 and the staging-loop catch at :328 keep throwing ManagedStoreError('recovery-required') but pass the KeystoreUnavailableError as cause when the caught error is or wraps one.

dataModelChanges.entity: Saved management opening (daemon start and request handlers)
dataModelChanges.details: Before: main awaited ensureDefaultManagedRoot for every registered repository before server.listen (src/daemon/index.ts:455-461), reading each repository's ticket key, rollback copies and every connection secret; request handlers assumed a missing service meant recovery/upgrade (owner, safeList) or an unopened managed registry (listConnectionsRpc returns []). After: the loop is deleted; closeDefaultManagedRoots stays in connectionOwners. Rule: a READ opens only an EXISTING managed root, a WRITE or capability probe may also initialize a fresh one. Concretely: owner() (src/daemon/connection-management-rpc.ts:46) awaits ensureDefaultManagedRoot(repoRoot) when savedManagementFor(repoRoot) is unset, swallowing the failure and then keeping its current recovery-required/upgrade-required decision unless the failure is a keystore refusal, which it rethrows so managementRejection reports 'secret-unavailable'; safeList() (:52) does the same only when the registry has a management marker; capabilities (:117) is unchanged (already on demand; failure suppresses mutation features). listConnectionsRpc (src/daemon/db-rpc.ts:79) awaits the open only when a transport is present and the registry has a management marker, and keeps returning [] on failure, logging the rejection code. saveConnection (src/daemon/db-rpc.ts:135) awaits the open for a registered root before reading savedManagementFor; a keystore refusal returns `{ error: 'secret-unavailable: ...' }`; any other failure falls through to today's legacy path. deleteConnection (src/daemon/db-rpc.ts:222) is unchanged: it refuses every managed registry from loaded.file._management and never needs an open service.

Before: initializeFreshManagedRoot wrote the parent directory, the state directory (a management marker), the owner lease, the snapshot and preparing.json (src/daemon/db/management-defaults.ts:25-40) and only then opened the ticket authority (:41), so a Keychain refusal left a marker and every later open failed as recovery-required. After: the ticket authority is opened right after the read-only checks (:20-24) and before the first write; a failure leaves the disk untouched; a later failure deletes the just-created ticket key best-effort.

Documented non-change, not a code change: withDriver -> savedConnectionResolver -> acquirePool -> DriverPool.reload -> loadConnections reads the committed db-connections.json and resolves only the used connection's secrets at driver build; it never read management state, so it never depended on the boot open (and already ran whenever that open failed). Journal recovery (CredentialGenerations.recover) never rewrites the registry; it only deletes refs the committed registry does not reference, so the registry a data tool reads is consistent whether or not recovery has run. The tools run on session workers; no worker-to-main route is added.

errorCases.scenario: The user denies the Keychain prompt for a repository's ticket key on its first management request
errorCases.detection: SavedTicketAuthority.open catches the rejected keystore.getKey and throws TicketError('secret-unavailable') inside openManagedRoot, which ensureDefaultManagedRoot propagates after forgetting the attempt
errorCases.response: owner() rethrows it, so managementRejection returns code 'secret-unavailable'; listConnectionsRpc logs the code and returns [] (array contract kept); saveConnection returns { error: 'secret-unavailable: Connection credentials are unavailable.' }; capabilities advertises no mutation features. The next request retries the open.
errorCases.userImpact: That request fails with 'Connection credentials are unavailable.'; the daemon and all non-connection work keep running; allowing the prompt on retry works.

errorCases.scenario: The Keychain refuses a rollback-copy or connection-secret read during openManagedRoot
errorCases.detection: The keystore wrapper in openManagedRoot (rollback read, enabled() secret reads) turns the rejected getKey into KeystoreUnavailableError; the enclosing open rethrows ManagedStoreError('recovery-required', { cause })
errorCases.response: ensureDefaultManagedRoot forgets the attempt; managementRejection sees the cause and reports 'secret-unavailable'.
errorCases.userImpact: Same as above: retryable, reported as unavailable credentials instead of a recovery demand.

errorCases.scenario: The Keychain refuses creating the ticket key while a fresh repository is initialised
errorCases.detection: SavedTicketAuthority.open({ adopted:false }), now the first side-effecting step of initializeFreshManagedRoot, throws TicketError('secret-unavailable')
errorCases.response: No directory, marker, snapshot, preparing.json or registry has been written; the error propagates and the attempt is forgotten. The next request runs a clean initialization.
errorCases.userImpact: No partial root, no recovery-required state; retrying works.

errorCases.scenario: A fresh initialization fails AFTER its ticket key was created (e.g. writer-fence proof fails, or a racing process published a registry)
errorCases.detection: Any throw in initializeFreshManagedRoot after SavedTicketAuthority.open
errorCases.response: As today the error propagates (recovery-required, or the racing writer's root is opened next time); additionally keystore.deleteKey for the abandoned db-management:v2:<registryId>:ticket-key is attempted; a failed delete is logged with the ref name only.
errorCases.userImpact: Unchanged outcome; at worst one unused Keychain item remains.

errorCases.scenario: A Keychain read or write fails while credentials are staged or checked during a saved upsert
errorCases.detection: The keystore wrapper in CredentialGenerations.current / stageSnapshot raises KeystoreUnavailableError, caught at the existing catch sites
errorCases.response: The catch sites still throw ManagedStoreError('recovery-required') (journal and assertReady semantics unchanged) but with the KeystoreUnavailableError as cause; managementRejection reports 'secret-unavailable'.
errorCases.userImpact: The save fails with 'Connection credentials are unavailable.' instead of 'requires recovery'; previous secrets are intact; any pending journal is handled exactly as today.

errorCases.scenario: A repository has a legacy unmanaged db-connections.json
errorCases.detection: initializeFreshManagedRoot's existing absent-registry check (before.missing false) throws recovery-required before any Keychain access
errorCases.response: ensureDefaultManagedRoot forgets the attempt; owner()/saveConnection keep today's legacy behaviour (upgrade-required / legacy write path); listConnectionsRpc and safeList do not open at all because there is no management marker.
errorCases.userImpact: Unchanged from today; no Keychain prompt.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Journal recovery never rewrites the registry; it only deletes refs the committed registry does not reference, and mutations stay refused while a journal is pending (assertReady).
ensureDefaultManagedRoot memoises one open per root and forgets a failed attempt so a later call retries.
A legacy unmanaged registry is never adopted online and is refused before any Keychain access.
The data-tool path reads only the committed registry and the used connection's secrets, on workers, without management state.
Client-facing rejections carry only a code and its fixed message; no secret or ref value is exposed.
deleteConnection refuses every managed registry from the file's _management field without an open service.

migration.stateBefore: At daemon start main awaits ensureDefaultManagedRoot for every registered repository before server.listen (src/daemon/index.ts:455-461), so each start reads every managed repository's ticket key, rollback copies and connection secrets and initialises a fresh managed root for every registered repository without a registry. initializeFreshManagedRoot writes its state directory, snapshot and preparing.json before obtaining the ticket key (src/daemon/db/management-defaults.ts:25-41). Keystore failures in CredentialGenerations and openManagedRoot surface as recovery-required with no cause (src/daemon/db/secrets.ts:212,236,242,328; src/daemon/db/management-startup.ts:53,85), and managementRejection cannot tell them apart (src/daemon/db/management.ts:62-68).
migration.stateAfter: Daemon start opens no managed root and touches no Keychain item. The main-thread management handlers open a repository on its first request through the memoised ensureDefaultManagedRoot (reads open only an existing managed root; writes and capability probes may initialise a fresh one). Fresh initialisation obtains the ticket key before writing to disk. Keystore failures keep their internal recovery-required semantics but carry a KeystoreUnavailableError cause, and clients receive 'secret-unavailable'. Data tools are unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional ErrorOptions cause to ManagedStoreError and the internal KeystoreUnavailableError; wrap the keystore port calls in CredentialGenerations and openManagedRoot so a thrown keystore error becomes the cause of the existing recovery-required error; teach managementRejection to report 'secret-unavailable' for that cause.

Reorder initializeFreshManagedRoot so the registryId is generated and SavedTicketAuthority.open runs before the first filesystem write, with best-effort deletion of that new ticket key on any later failure.
Add the on-demand ensureDefaultManagedRoot call to owner(), safeList(), listConnectionsRpc and saveConnection per the read/write rule; leave capabilities and deleteConnection as they are.
Delete the boot loop in main; keep closeDefaultManagedRoots in connectionOwners for shutdown.

migration.backwardCompat: No on-disk or wire format change: existing managed roots, legacy registries and Keychain items are used as they are, and the daemon can be rolled back to the previous build at any time. 'secret-unavailable' is an existing wire code that clients already render; some failures that were reported as 'recovery-required' are now reported as 'secret-unavailable'. Repositories without a registry are no longer initialised at daemon start but on their first saved write or capability probe; until then db.listConnections returns [] for them, which is the same answer an empty managed registry gave.

alternativesConsidered.name: Open on first management request through the existing memoised opener
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Delete the boot loop; the main-thread management handlers that need an open service await ensureDefaultManagedRoot first; fresh initialization takes its ticket key before writing to disk; keystore failures carry their cause to managementRejection. Data tools unchanged.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Boot: remove the for-loop at src/daemon/index.ts:455-461 (closeDefaultManagedRoots stays registered for shutdown). On demand: the main-thread handlers that need an open service await the memoised ensureDefaultManagedRoot(root) (forgets failures) and then read savedManagementFor(root). Callers: owner() and safeList() in src/daemon/connection-management-rpc.ts, listConnectionsRpc (only when a transport is present and the registry carries a management marker, so a plain listing of an unmanaged or absent registry never creates state or touches the Keychain) and saveConnection (registered root) in src/daemon/db-rpc.ts; capabilities already does this. deleteConnection needs no open: it already refuses every managed registry from the file's _management field. Fresh init: in initializeFreshManagedRoot, generate registryId and call SavedTicketAuthority.open (adopted:false) right after the absent-registry and marker checks and before the first chmod/mkdir/write; on any later failure delete that freshly created ticket key best-effort. Cause: ManagedStoreError gains an optional ErrorOptions cause; the keystore port calls in CredentialGenerations.current/stage/prepareRemoval and openManagedRoot's rollback and enabled() reads wrap a thrown keystore error as KeystoreUnavailableError and the catch sites keep throwing recovery-required but with that cause; managementRejection reports 'secret-unavailable' when the error or its cause is a KeystoreUnavailableError. Data tools: unchanged, because they never read management state and journal recovery never rewrites the registry they read.
pros: Smallest change that meets all four points; reuses ensureDefaultManagedRoot's memo and retry and the capabilities precedent
No new thread transport; every caller already runs on the main thread where the memo lives
No Keychain access at daemon start; a listing of an unmanaged or absent registry never touches the Keychain
Internal recovery semantics unchanged (still recovery-required internally), only the client-facing code improves
cons: Opening a managed root on demand still reads that repo's ticket key, rollback copies and every connection secret (enabled()), so the first use of each repository can still prompt once per item; the one-prompt vault is the separate later Story
Repositories created fresh at boot today are now created on first saved upsert/capabilities instead

alternativesConsidered.name: a1 plus a recovery gate on the data-tool path
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As a1, and additionally make DriverPool.reload refuse a managed registry whose preparation journal has pending records, as a metadata-only check on the worker.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Everything in a1. In addition, DriverPool.reloadNow (src/daemon/db/pool.ts:70) checks, when file._management is present, whether the PreparationJournal for that registryId has pending records (a file read, no Keychain) and throws ConnectionUseError('recovery-required') if so, so a data tool never runs against a root whose staging has not been recovered. Works on any thread without a worker-to-main route because it only reads files.
pros: Data tools never run while a staging journal is pending
No Keychain access and no cross-thread route on the data path
cons: Changes data-tool behaviour that the boot open never provided: today a data tool already runs when the boot open failed, and with on-demand opening a pending journal is only recovered by a management request, so a repo whose user only uses data tools would stay refused indefinitely
Adds protection without a consistency benefit: recover() only deletes refs the committed registry does not reference, so the registry the tool reads is consistent with or without recovery
Reaches into PreparationJournal's private file layout from the pool
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Same as a1 plus a gate that adds a new failure mode without protecting the data the tools read.

alternativesConsidered.name: Make savedManagementFor itself lazy and async
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Turn savedManagementFor(root) into an async accessor that opens the root on first call, so every reader opens implicitly.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Change savedManagementFor in src/daemon/db/management.ts to `async savedManagementFor(root)` that awaits ensureDefaultManagedRoot when no service is installed, and update every caller (ensureDefaultManagedRoot's own early return, the RPC readers, deleteConnection) to await it.
pros: No reader can forget to open
cons: Creates a call cycle (ensureDefaultManagedRoot uses savedManagementFor for its early return) that must be broken with a second sync accessor
Opens roots for readers that do not need an open service (deleteConnection, no-transport listings), touching the Keychain needlessly
Hides a Keychain-reaching side effect behind a getter name
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Opens roots for readers that need no service, touching the Keychain more than a1, and creates an accessor cycle.

alternativesConsidered.name: Keep eager opening but run it after the socket listens
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Move the boot loop after server.listen so the socket opens first, still opening every registered root in the background.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Move src/daemon/index.ts:455-461 after server.listen and run it without awaiting, logging failures as today.
pros: One-line change; socket no longer waits on the Keychain
cons: Does not meet the fix intent: every daemon start still reads every repository's ticket key and connection secrets and prompts for each, whether or not connections are used
Requests racing the background open still see an unopened root
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Does not meet the fix intent.

openQuestions: Scope refinement (stakeholder decision 'A', 2026-11-05, after design review round 3 of this LLD): ISSUE-fefa97b991537da7 fix intent 3 (at most one Keychain prompt per daemon run for every saved credential, including tool configuration, notify and web keys) is NOT delivered here; it moves to a separate later tracked Story (a connection vault). Until it ships, the first management request for a managed repository can still prompt once per Keychain item of that repository (ticket key, rollback copies, connection secrets), but a daemon start prompts for nothing.

Carry-over lessons for that vault Story from rounds 2-3 of this LLD: use a separate Keychain service or enforce a reserved account across keys.get/set/delete/list; do not inventory legacy items with keytar findCredentials (on macOS it reads every secret and returns empty pairs on a refused read); define a rollback for a failed or partial migration.
